questions.question: The Arya Samaj was founded by Dayanand Saraswati in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
• Arya Samaj Foundation: 1875
  • Founder: Swami Dayanand Saraswati in Bombay (motto: 'Go back to the Vedas').

questions.question: Banabhatta was a court poet of Harshavardhana, who wrote a book called:
questions.solution:
• Harshacharita: Harshacharita
  • Author: Banabhatta also wrote 'Kadambari', the world's first novel.

questions.question: Which of the following Buddhist sages had initiated the Indo-Greek king Menander into Buddhism?
questions.solution:
• Nagasena: Nagasena
  • Dialogue: Their conversation is recorded in the famous text 'Milindapanho'.

questions.question: The Rashtrakuta king who conquered the Cholas was:
questions.solution:
• Krishna III: Krishna III
  • Battle: He defeated the Cholas at the Battle of Takkolam in 949 CE.

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative on the given statements based on Ashoka’s Lion capital and India’s State Emblem.

Statement I: In the original Ashoka’s Lion Capital, there are four lions mounted back-to-back on a circular abacus that itself rests on a bell-shaped lotus.

Statement II: The State Emblem is an adaptation of the Lion Capital of Asoka at Sarnath in which the bell-shaped lotus was omitted.
questions.option_2: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.option_3: Neither Statement I nor Statement II is true.
questions.solution:
• Lion Capital Statements: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
  • Emblem: Adopted on Jan 26, 1950, showing three lions (the fourth being hidden).

questions.question: Pitt’s India Act was passed in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
• Pitt’s India Act: 1784
  • Purpose: To rectify the defects of the Regulating Act of 1773.

questions.question: Under which Act did the individual members of the Executive Council have their own portfolio?
questions.solution:
• Portfolio System: The Indian Councils Act of 1861
  • Detail: Introduced by Lord Canning, laying the foundation of cabinet government in India.

questions.question:
With reference to the city administration of Mauryan Empire, consider the following statements.

a) Megasthenes put light on the Mauryan city administration.

b) The city council was divided into six committees.

c) City administration was well planned.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Mauryan Administration: a, b, c
  • Fact: Megasthenes mentions 6 committees of 5 members each overseeing city functions.

questions.question: North Indian architecture is called:
questions.solution:
• Nagara Style: Nagara style
  • Key Feature: Curvilinear towers called Shikharas.

questions.question: To study the buildings and structures of the Harappan civilisation, a teacher should take his students on a field trip to which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
• IVC States: Gujrat and Rajasthan
  • Sites: Lothal and Dholavira (Gujarat), Kalibangan (Rajasthan).

questions.question: Where was the first Headquarters of the Theosophical Society established in India?
questions.solution:
• Theosophical HQ: Adyar
  • 1882: Moved from Bombay to Adyar (Madras) under Olcott and Blavatsky.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the Medhi part in Buddhist structure?
questions.option_1: The circular terrace between the railing and dome
questions.option_2: Ceremonial gateways in front of stupas
questions.option_3: A low wall to enclose the structure
questions.option_4: The umbrella-shaped structure placed at the top of the structure
questions.solution:
• Medhi: The circular terrace between the railing and dome
  • Architecture: It serves as an upper circumambulation path (Pradakshina Patha).

questions.question: Which of the following architectural features were NOT a part of Harappan cities?
questions.solution:
• Harappan Features (NOT): Industrial and commercial buildings
  • Correction: While they had workshops, Harappan cities are famous for residential planning and granaries, not large separate 'industrial' buildings like modern factories.

questions.question: Which of the following edicts of King Ashoka describes the Kalinga war?
questions.solution:
• Rock Edict XIII: Rock edict XIII
  • Impact: It describes the suffering of the Kalinga war and Ashoka's remorse.

questions.question: Chandragupta Maurya’s capital was:
questions.solution:
• Mauryan Capital: Pataliputra
  • City: Described by Megasthenes as a massive city surrounded by a wooden wall with 570 towers.

questions.question: When was the voting age in India reduced from 21 years to 18 years?
questions.solution:
• Voting Age 18: 1989
  • Amendment: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 (implemented in 1989).

questions.question: Which of the following Mahajanapadas emerged as the most powerful at the end of a prolonged conflict for supremacy?
questions.solution:
• Magadha Supremacy: Magadha
  • Reason: Favorable geography, iron mines, and ambitious rulers like Bimbisara and Mahapadma Nanda.

questions.question: Kautilya has mentioned the concept of Saptanga Rajya to understand the State with seven organs and one of them is Danda, which means:
questions.solution:
• Danda: Force
  • Saptanga: The seven limbs include Swami (King), Amatya (Ministers), Janapada (Territory), Durga (Fort), Kosha (Treasury), Danda (Force/Army), and Mitra (Ally).

questions.question: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew which of the following dynasties of ancient India to establish the Mauryan empire?
questions.solution:
• Mauryan Foundation: Nanda
  • Event: Chandragupta defeated Dhana Nanda with the help of Chanakya.

questions.question: Itmad-ud-daula tomb is situated in which of the following cities?
questions.solution:
• Itmad-ud-daula: Agra
  • Fact: Built by Nur Jahan for her father. It was the first Mughal structure to use white marble and extensive Pietra Dura.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct explanation of painting and sculpture of Ajanta and Elora caves?
questions.option_1: They are depiction of Buddhist religious art.
questions.option_2: They are representations of medieval Islamic art.
questions.option_3: They are symbolic representations of Gods in Judaism.
questions.option_4: They are designed in Persian art form.
questions.solution:
• Ajanta and Elora: They are depiction of Buddhist religious art.
  • Note: While Ellora is multi-religious (Hindu, Buddhist, Jain), Ajanta is exclusively Buddhist.

questions.question: The sculptures under the Gandhara School of Art were made of stone, terracotta and _________.
questions.solution:
• Gandhara Art: clay
  • Medium: Also used Stucco (a type of plaster) alongside grey schist stone.

questions.question: Which of the following administrative units was introduced during the reign of Shahjahan?
questions.solution:
• Chakla: Chakla
  • Admin: An administrative unit larger than a Pargana but smaller than a Subah.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations was NOT associated with Vinayak Damodar Savarkar?
questions.solution:
• Savarkar (NOT): Servants of India Society
  • Correction: Servants of India Society was founded by Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the rule of Chandragupta II?

A) Chandragupta II adopted the title ‘Vikramaditya’.

B)Kalidasa and Amarasimha were part of his court.
questions.solution:
• Chandragupta II: Both A and B
  • Legacy: Known for the 'Iron Pillar of Delhi' and the peak of Sanskrit literature.
